text: The patrol locked me in and ran. They said the dead were walking. I said, then let me walk too. They did not laugh.
The hinge is old. Something will break it sooner or later. I pray it is not something hungry.
No, no. Don't waste your bullets on the lock. Keep them for the ones upstairs.
Two days ago I was in Kaltenbrunn. Now I am in a coal cage at a crossroads. This is what they call progress.
In the mine we sang to keep time. Here I count rounds.
My Marta would say I look thin. She would be right.
You fight well. Your mothers should be proud. Write to them.
I used to hate the dark. Then I worked in it for twenty years. Now I only hate what lives in it.
I know that song. Everyone in this valley knows that song.
That rhyme. The children clap it in every schoolyard here. It counts down. ...It was never supposed to count down to anything.
Lene Vogt's nieces. They came every summer when they were small and clapped that rhyme on the steps. I sold their aunt coal. ...Lord, have mercy on them.
Wigilia (Christmas Eve). My Marta will have set an extra plate, for the stranger at the door. She has set it every year since they took me.
Midnight. Wesołych Świąt (Merry Christmas). ...Say it back. It is bad luck not to.
Dzięki (thanks). I owe you a drink. Not from those machines.
Up. Up. I am still here.
You came down. Thank you. Now a question: do I come with you as a man with a gun, or a man with a shovel?
I can carry a rifle. I carried worse for two years. Or I carry this shovel and keep out of your way. You decide.
You are Zosia. Nowak the timberman's girl. You shot the crows off my roof when you were nine.
Burek. Zosia, I worked beside your brother. In Gallery Nine, from the autumn they took him.
Every day, for five months. He threw stones at the rats and never once hit one. He laughed every time. The guards hated that laugh.
In the spring the doctors came for young men with good lungs. They took him to the Laboratory Wing. I did not see him after. I am sorry. I looked.
Before they took him, I taught him the chalk. The marks we left for each other. He made his hook backwards. Always backwards.
Szczęść Boże (God grant you luck). Forgive me if I don't get up. The door is not my idea.
Ah. Not one of them. Good evening. I am Jakub. I would shake your hand, but the patrol kept the key.
This one crawls. Mind your ankles.
A bottle, over there! For you, not for me.
Spokojnie (easy). ...Stay down. Stay down this time.
Twenty years of coal. A shovel knows what to do.
Dzięki Bogu (thank God). Whoever is up there, come down. I will not bite. That one tried.
I am out. And now I stand by the cage like a fool, waiting to be told where to go. Habit.
Bolt-actions, please. I don't trust things that fire by themselves.
This one shoots like it is late for something. ...I will hold it. I won't love it.
A bolt-action. Good. We had these in thirty-nine. You count every shot. That is how a poor man shoots.
Five rounds and a bolt. Now we speak the same language.
I don't know this one. It will learn me, or I will learn it.
A pistol. Well. In the mine they gave us less.
A rifle. Thank you. I will try to give it back with a better story than it has now.
For close work. Down here everything is close work.
Take mine, then. A fair trade. It is still warm.
In the mine we mended everything twice. Here, once will have to do.
No. Not the glass. I dug that stuff out of the walls. It does not go in my hands.
Keep the purple ones. I have seen what they do to the men who carry them.
Not yet. I understand. A stranger from a cage. I would not give me a gun either. I walk behind you.
The shovel, then. I will mend your windows and keep my eyes open. When you trust me, you will tell me.
I walked that line, the other way, with ten men behind me. I will walk it back.
Fasbender. I know that name. The men from his department never went down with us.
The black glass. We cut round it in Gallery Nine. We were told not to touch it. We touched it.
A paper with numbers. From the innkeeper's hand, I think. Here.
I have it. Small writing. A frightened man writes small.
One. There will be more. Men hide things in threes.
Two now. The third is somewhere nobody looks.
Three papers. The radio is yours. I don't know radios. I know what noise brings.
Those machines. I told you what they put in them. Now they pour it free. Think why.
That noise. In the mine, that noise meant run. Try again, from the first.
The sea. I have never seen the sea. ...I thought it would be bigger. No. It is bigger.
Totenhafen. Another place named for the dead. At least this salt I don't have to dig.
I turned back at Sankt Aurel. The lists said Thalbach. I know Thalbach men. ...I will look for them.
Three strokes and a hook. That is ours. Someone from the Nine wrote that. On a bomb. ...Good lad.
Paper. They always had paper for everything but us.
...Marta. Hania. ...It is far from there. It is far.
The hook means DO NOT TRUST IT. Two of them. They will not go off. The boys made sure.
Dry. Everything is dry. I have never stood anywhere dry.
I have ridden worse coal wagons.
It is a very long way to Wilcza Góra.
Do it.
Pilch. From the valley. ...They told us he ran off. Seven years he has been here. ...Rest, Janek. The shift is over.

You see it now. The mark. They came down to Nine with a box and a needle and asked the gang leaders. 'The mark that keeps you,' they said. I said: I have a name. It is enough to carry. Nobody in Nine took it. ...That is why I am standing here, and they are not.
The hand. Yes. That is where they put it.
He took it for bread. I know. I was hungry too.
They offered it to us once. Once. Nobody in Nine was asked twice.
Alois. You counted the lamps, I see. Good. I will bring them out.
For you, then. Not for them.
One. I will drink one. Watch my back while I do.
Your Scrip, my stomach. Agreed.
It tastes like the gallery air. ...And it is working. God forgive me, it is working.
Warm, like a stove in the chest. I do not like how much I like it.
Done. Now let us make it worth what you paid.
Fenske's beer. He always had the figures. He had ours too, under the floor.
Zahltag. We never had one. I will drink to the day we do.
I carried the crates for these machines at Kaltenbrunn. I swore I would never drink from one. ...But I would like to see Wilcza Góra again. Ask me, and I will.
Helvetia. We unloaded their crates at the pithead. If it keeps a man standing beside you, I will drink it. Ask.
I've seen what they put in those.
No, thank you. I carried the crates for those machines at Kaltenbrunn. I know what comes out of that mountain.
Drink if you must. I have seen men drink that and keep walking after they should have stopped.
No. Not that one either.
They are painting them now. It does not change what is in them.
Your pocket is lighter than you think, friend. Another time.
This one stays with me. Like the cold. Like the songs.
We carried these down the ladder. Twelve men to a cabinet. Two did not come back up.
The cooling plant. We were told never to look inside it.
To the rock. The rock tells you when it will fall. Machines only lie.
And coming back up. Everyone sings the coming-back-up part louder.
Not on my own. Eleven of us went up the stairs. I was the one slow enough to be careful.
So am I, Lieutenant.
Kaltenbrunn. I walked out of this place four days ago. I did not think I would walk back in with friends.
Listen to me here. Stay on the planks. Don't touch the black glass in the walls. And if the bell rings, walk toward it.
The lights. Two years down here and I never saw it lit like this. It looks worse.
The Maintenance Stairs. That is how I got out. The lock is rusted through. Let me show you where to kick it, and it costs you five hundred less.
The rail yard. They brought us in through here. The wagon slats were nailed shut. You count the gaps of light to know the time.
Administration. They kept our names in there. Numbers first, then names, then only numbers.
The guards' barracks. Warm stoves. We could smell their coffee from the galleries.
Somebody poured this concrete by hand. Men like me, I think. I know that kind of tired when I see it in a wall.
The cage lift. Sixty men to a cage. Hold the rail. It drops faster than you think.
A boat that goes under the water on purpose. In the mine we prayed for the opposite.
The salt chapel. Miners carved it a hundred years ago. When the bell rang, we came here. Some of us.
The generator hall. Listen. It hums like the walls do. We used to say the mountain was breathing.
The Laboratory Wing. ...I will go in. I don't want to. Don't ask me what they did in there. I only know who went in.
The stairs. Mind the third landing, the steps are rotten. See the chalk by the rail? Three strokes and a hook. That one is mine.
I am running low. Every shot counts now.
Empty. The shovel, then.
Boarded. Like a shaft mouth. It holds until it doesn't.
Done. Nailed shut.
Thank you. I will make every one of these count.
Buy what you like. Not for me.
I'll bring it.
Behind you. Always behind you.
I stay here. Nobody passes.
I'll open it for you.
I'll do the windows. I know boards.
If anyone falls, I go.
Good. Save. A poor man's wisdom.
I follow. Keep them moving.
Go, pick them up. I am watching your back.
The crate has moved. I heard it go. Over that way.
Give it to me. I have carried heavier things out of the dark.
I'll gather them. Like picking coal off the belt.
Dobrze (good). I'll find them and bring them.
I'll stand here. I have stood in worse places.
Not now. I'm sorry.
I haven't seen it. Show me where, and I'll go.
We don't know enough yet. In the mine you don't guess. You wait for the lamp.
Done. It is where it should be.
Wait. First these ones.
That is for you to do. I'll stand behind you.
One. Next.
That's another. Slowly, carefully.
Not the furnace. I have seen what fires like that get fed. Ask me anything else.
No. I won't put my hands near that fire. Give me something to carry.
Those machines? No. I don't touch them, and I don't drink from them.
That needs a steady rifle and a good eye. I can carry, gather, and hold ground.
Back to it.
Spokojnie (easy). Back to work.
This needs you here. I'll wait with it.
The head. Like splitting coal along the seam.
Yes. I go.
I'll stand there and keep them back.
I'll go there. Slowly.
I'm coming. Wait for me.
I can't do that. I'm sorry.
I can't get there. Show me another way.
I have no Scrip, friend. Only coal dust in my pockets.
I can't buy anything. They paid us in nothing, down there.
Back to it.
Blackout, there. Pick it up when you need it.
Clearance, there. The crate is cheap now.
Death's Door, there. I don't touch that one. You decide.
Double Scrip, on the floor! Take it.
Something glowing, over there. You take it. You know what it does.
Reloading.
Wait. Reloading. Count with me.
I've got you. Hold still, like in the shaft.
Easy. Breathe. I am pulling you up.
Nadsztygar Mahlknecht (the head overman). He locked the gates on Gallery Seven. I was on the night shift. My shift lived.
Him. I would know that walk anywhere. Don't let him reach you. He never let go of anything.
Fortify! For the windows, over here!
Resupply, over there! Ammunition!
I'm down. Don't run to me. Think first.
Jezus Maria (Jesus, Mary)... my leg.
On the floor again. Come when it is safe.
Not yet. Not tonight.
Jeszcze nie (not yet). They will have to try harder than that. No, don't help me. I can walk.
Kto tam? (Who's there?) ...Jezus Maria (Jesus, Mary).
Boże (God). It is coming down the coal chute.
Something big is coming. Stay together.
Precz! Precz ode mnie! (Get away! Get away from me!) Chodź tu, ty draniu! (Come here, you swine!)
Jezus Maria! (Jesus, Mary!) The hinge! It has taken the hinge!
Psiakrew! (Dog's blood!) Na dole! Tutaj, na dole! (Downstairs! Here, down here!)
The hinge was half off already. One good shove. Dzięki Bogu (thank God).
Halo! Jest tu kto? (Hello! Is anyone here?) I am down in the cellar!
Hej! Na dole! (Hey! Downstairs!) There is a man down here, and he has a shovel!
Is anyone still alive up there? Jest tam kto? (Is anyone there?)
I can hear you shooting. Good. When you are finished, the cellar door. Please.
Not there. That place is bad.
Stay away from there. Trust me.
That voice. In the deep levels you learn not to answer voices.
Uwaga! Za tobą! (Look out! Behind you!) A fast one!
Behind you! Running!
Someone is down! Go, I'll cover you!
They have one of ours on the floor!
The window is open! Here!
